transcript:
Meeting Header
Date: 2027-08-25
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 56 minutes (recording)
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Samira Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Thompson (Redwood CSM), Dr. Rachel Nguyen (Catalyst Care CTO), Carlos Mendes (VP Eng), Leah Ortiz (PM), Tom Reyes (Security)

Agenda:
- Introductions / goals for onboarding
- Technical baseline (stack, infra, security requirements)
- Success criteria, timeline, and pilot scope
- Next steps & responsibilities

Summary:
Quick kickoff for Catalyst Care to onboard onto Redwood (hosted -> Dedicated trial discussion). Primary goals: integrate Redwood text generation for patient-facing triage assistant, meet p99 latency targets < 450ms for 1-2 token increments in interactive flows, validate SOC2/SAML for enterprise rollout, and run initial perf tests on a sample workload.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we, we really appreciate you all making time. I'm Alex, AE at Redwood, with Samira our SE and Maya CSM. How's everyone doing?
[00:05] Dr. Rachel Nguyen: Morning, thanks Alex. Super excited to get started, we've been looking at the docs — Carlos and I will drive the engineering piece.
[00:12] Carlos Mendes: Hi all. Quick note, we're evaluating a couple vendors but Redwood's latency numbers look promising. Wanted to make sure the onboarding process is straightforward.
[00:20] Maya Thompson: Totally. Today we'll run through the plan, confirm requirements (SSO, retention, region), and set up the pilot scope.
[00:28] Samira Patel: For the SE piece I'll ask about existing infra — are you planning to use Hosted first or go straight to Dedicated / VPC?
[00:34] Leah Ortiz: We're thinking hosted for the first 4-6 weeks to iterate, then a Dedicated pool if everything's stable. Is that a common path?
[00:40] Alex Kim: Yeah that's pretty normal. Hosted for quick iteration then Dedicated when you want isolation and predictable throughput. We'll show both options in the proposal.
[00:47] Tom Reyes: From security side, we need SOC2 Type II evidence, SSO with SAML, and KMS integration for keys. Any gotchas?
[00:55] Maya Thompson: We have a SOC2 package, SAML guides, and KMS integration playbooks — I'll share those after the call. We also have an on-prem option if keys need to stay in-house.
[01:03] Samira Patel: On the performance side, can you describe expected traffic patterns? e.g., avg tokens per request, expected concurrency and qps?
[01:10] Carlos Mendes: For the triage assistant, typical session is 8-12 turns, about 20 tokens generated per turn on average. Peak concurrent sessions we expect maybe 30-40, QPS ~15-20 for the first phase.
[01:20] Samira Patel: Okay that helps. Our initial suggestion is to start with hosted small instances to validate prompt shapes and then run a benchmarking pass to recommend batching and quantization profiles.
[01:28] Dr. Rachel Nguyen: We care a lot about p99 latency for the interactive flow, target is under 450ms. We saw some benchmarks in your docs but want to run our own.
[01:36] Alex Kim: Absolutely, we'll run an end-to-end benchmark with your prompts. Samira will lead that. We'll need a sample prompt set and a traffic script.
[01:43] Leah Ortiz: Onboarding timeline — we'd like production by end of Q4. Is that realistic?
[01:48] Maya Thompson: Yes, that's doable. Typical onboarding takes 6-10 weeks depending on pilot scope and security review. With SOC2/SPs cleared and a small Dedicated trial we can hit your timeline.
[01:56] Tom Reyes: A question on data retention — can you confirm retention windows and whether customer logs can be disabled for Hosted?
[02:02] Alex Kim: Hosted defaults to short retention, and we have controls for disabling certain logs; for strict controls Dedicated/Private is the option. We'll include exact retention policies in the security packet.
[02:10] Carlos Mendes: Any IP/eval sandbox for us to run the pilot without touching PHI? We need to be careful.
[02:17] Maya Thompson: Recommend you scrub PHI for the pilot; we can also provide a private trial environment or sign an addendum if needed. I'll follow up with legal touchpoints.
[02:25] Samira Patel: Technical deep dive — do you have any existing GPUs or inference stack? Are you running LLMs in-house anywhere?
[02:31] Carlos Mendes: We're not hosting models; everything's currently in-house rule-based systems. We'll want Redwood to handle inference.
[02:36] Samira Patel: Great. For integration options we support REST/SDKs, streaming responses, and function/tool calling. We'll recommend a streaming approach for the triage UI to reduce perceived latency.
[02:46] Leah Ortiz: Integration-wise, our frontend team uses TypeScript and React; backend is Node services on GCP. Any sample SDKs for that?
[02:52] Alex Kim: Yep, we have TypeScript SDKs and quickstarts for Node. I'll share a repo link.
[02:57] [05:00] Samira Patel: (later) For the benchmark we want 3 things: your prompt set, a sample corpus for caching tests, and a traffic script that emulates your concurrency. We'll run baseline on Hosted then try a Dedicated instance with our batching.
[05:12] Carlos Mendes: We'll aim to get that to you by EOW.
[05:18] Maya Thompson: Security follow-up: Tom, do you need an NDA amendment or anything before we share SOC2 artifact?
[05:23] Tom Reyes: A short data processing addendum would be ideal.
[05:27] Maya Thompson: I'll loop legal.
[05:30] [15:00] Alex Kim: Pricing — for Hosted we'll send per-token tiers and for Dedicated we can present monthly reserved capacity. We'll include sample cost modeling for your expected qps.
[15:10] Leah Ortiz: On success metrics, besides latency we want cost per session under $0.03 for the live pilot. Can you model that?
[15:18] Samira Patel: We'll put together a model based on tokens-per-turn and expected sessions; Dedicated usually helps with unit cost once you have consistent load.
[15:26] Dr. Rachel Nguyen: One more for reliability — what's your fallback during outages? Do you provide model variant fallbacks or multi-region?
[15:33] Alex Kim: Yes, smart routing with fallbacks to compatible model variants and multi-region routing are available. For enterprise we can set SLA-backed Dedicated clusters.
[15:40] Carlos Mendes: On SSO, we use Okta. SAML is required.
[15:45] Maya Thompson: Okta is supported; we'll send SAML guides and a test plan.
[15:50] [30:00] Samira Patel: Technical note — when we run perf tests, we'll also exercise KV cache/prefix caching. That often yields 20-40% token cost reduction for repeated prefixes in triage flows.
[30:10] Alex Kim: Great. Any blockers on your side?
[30:14] Carlos Mendes: Legal needs the DPA + SOC2, and security wants more info on KMS; otherwise we can begin the pilot planning.
[30:22] Maya Thompson: I'll own the document collection; Alex will send pricing and trial proposal; Samira will schedule the perf window.
[30:29] Leah Ortiz: We'll schedule a technical deep-dive next week if possible.
[30:34] Alex Kim: Cool — Samira, what windows do you have next week?
[30:38] Samira Patel: Tue/Wed morning PST are open; I'll send a Doodle.
[30:42] [45:00] Tom Reyes: Quick compliance Q — how do you handle audit logs for admin actions in Dedicated? Are they shipped to customer KMS or stored in Redwood sys?
[45:10] Maya Thompson: Dedicated supports audit log export; we can ship logs to your cloud bucket or forward via syslog; encryption at rest with customer-managed keys is supported.
[45:22] Tom Reyes: Good, that'll work.
[45:26] Alex Kim: Alright, to recap real quick: 1) Redwood sends onboarding guide, SAML + SOC2 artifacts, and pricing; 2) Catalyst Care provides prompt set and traffic script; 3) SE runs benchmark and shares results; 4) schedule deep-dive next week.
[45:42] Dr. Rachel Nguyen: That aligns with our expectations. Looking forward to the proposal.
[45:47] Alex Kim: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up by email.

End of recording
